The check passes today with zero warnings when `-W error::DeprecationWarning` is enabled, yet the transcript's second run (without the flag) shows the 2 warnings are still present. This means the check cannot distinguish "work done" from "untouched"—it already passes before any fix is applied. A valid check would need to detect the warnings under normal conditions (e.g., `pytest ... -q 2>&1 | grep -c DeprecationWarning` returning 0, or running without `-W error` and asserting zero warnings in the summary).
